title: Shapes and boiling points of group 15 hydrides
stem: Ammonia, NH₃, and phosphine, PH₃, are both hydrides of group 15 elements. Ammonia boils at −33 °C and phosphine at −88 °C. Hydrogen cyanide, HCN, is a linear molecule.

parts.label: a
parts.prompt: Deduce the electron domain geometry and the molecular geometry of NH₃, and estimate its H–N–H bond angle.

parts.label: b
parts.prompt: Explain why the bond angle in NH₃ is smaller than the bond angle in CH₄.
markscheme: NH₃ has a lone pair on N / CH₄ has no lone pairs
lone pair–bonding pair repulsion is greater than bonding pair–bonding pair repulsion, so the bonding pairs are pushed closer together

parts.label: c
parts.prompt: Explain why ammonia has a higher boiling point than phosphine even though phosphine has more electrons.
markscheme: N is highly electronegative and small, with a lone pair, so N–H…N hydrogen bonds form / P is not electronegative enough
PH₃ has only London forces (and weak dipole–dipole forces), which are weaker overall / more energy needed to separate NH₃ molecules
parts.notes: Do not award marks for answers that refer to breaking covalent bonds on boiling.

parts.label: d
parts.prompt: State the number of σ and π bonds in HCN and the hybridization of the carbon atom.
